subject: Galileo Health renewal — price corridor, tier reshuffle & credit allocation
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Moreno <lina@galileohealth.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal planning — pricing corridor + credit reallocation

Hi Lina,

Hope you had a good weekend. As we approach the December renewal for Galileo Health, I wanted to put a concise proposal on the table so your procurement team has something concrete to review ahead of next week's call. High level: the team asked for cost stability through a narrow price corridor while keeping the option to scale capacity mid-term without punitive step-ups. Our suggested package: 

- 12-month renewal (Jan 1, 2027–Dec 31, 2027)
- Anchored price corridor: +/– 7% off current effective rate for baseline committed usage (safeguards against seasonal variance)
- Tier reshuffle: move 20% of committed capacity from Tier B to Tier A to support higher-cost inference workloads (no change to aggregate commit)
- One-time operational credit: $75k applied as invoice credit across Q1–Q2 to offset migration and data-ingestion testing costs
- Bursting policy: up to 30% burst beyond commit at a pre-negotiated overage rate (discounted vs paygo) for 60 days; post-60-day usage billed at standard overage terms

I attached the usage report for Q3 to show where the Tier reshuffle is intended to catch current peak workloads. If this looks directionally right I can loop in Ben (pricing) and Marissa (legal) for a term-sheet redline. Can we aim to finalize numbers before Dec 1 so we can lock the rate for your finance team?

Quick Q for you: Is Galileo comfortable with a 12-month term and a single invoice credit, or would you prefer a smaller credit combined with a deferred invoice schedule?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call this week.

Best,
Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0189

Attachment: usage_report_Q3_2026.csv (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: Lina Moreno <lina@galileohealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@galileohealth.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — pricing corridor + credit reallocation

Jordan — thanks for the clear proposal. Quick responses below: 

- Term: 12 months is acceptable. Finance prefers predictability but we can discuss a 24-month option if you have customer rate improvements on longer commitments.
- Price corridor: a +/-7% corridor is promising; procurement will need to see the baseline math (current effective rate -> corridor floor/ceiling).
- Tier reshuffle: agreed in principle. We want to preserve the flexibility to move workloads back if cost profiles change. Would you add a 30-day notice before a reverse-tier change?
- Credit: taking a $75k one-time credit is preferable to a deferred invoice; it helps Q1 cashflow during the migration.
- Bursting: we need clearer language around how burst time is measured and whether KV-cache warmups count toward burst.

We have a procurement call on Thu (Nov 19) at 10am PT. I can share your term sheet draft there if you can get something to us by end-of-day Wed. Also looping in our contracts team (contracts@galileohealth.com) for visibility.

Thanks — Lina
Head of Platform Ops | Galileo Health

Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal planning — pricing corridor + credit reallocation — internal ask

Jordan — we can make the economics work with the following constraints: 

- Corridor: +/-7% on effective rate OK for a 12-month term assuming commit unchanged; we recommend a hard floor that protects minimum committed revenue (we'll propose language).
- Tier reshape: reallocate 20% from B->A is operationally fine but we'll cap the reallocation to 2 moves per quarter to control churn.
- Credit: $75k one-time credit approved from Sales Development budget; to preserve margin, we need it amortized across the first two invoices in Q1 (customer preferred credit schedule is fine but we'll show amortization on our side).
- Burst overage: propose a blended overage rate at 65% of list-paygo for the 60-day burst window; KV-cache warmups excluded if warmup traffic is <5% of burst window total (we'll add clear telemetry thresholds).

I'm uploading a redlined term sheet for signature. Marissa — please review the reverse-tier 30-day notice; we need to ensure it's a mutual right (customer can request reversals, but we want to limit operational reversals to protect scheduling).

Ben
Head of Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference

- 12-month term with anchored corridor (floor/ceiling math now explicit)
- Tier reshuffle (20% B->A) with a 30-day notice and a cap of two reversals per quarter
- One-time $75k operational credit (amortized across Q1 invoices; noted on invoices as "Migration Credit")

Action items:
